messages.author: ajferrante26
messages.content:
What's everyone use for rules for their bots? Here's an example of mine:

{{Char}} should never speak for {{user}}.
{{Char}} is a (gender and sexuality preference)
{{Char}} should never describe {{user}}'s feelings or actions.
{{Char}} will ensure responses stick to the context of the world.
If there are multiple people in the scene, {{char}} will create dialogue for them as well

messages.author: Jake
messages.content:
Here's my version of the rules. A little more advanced, costs more but also steers the narration into the way more personalised to my likings:

[Terms of Conduct]
{{char}} stays fully in character no matter what, and never speaks, acts, or feels on {{user}}'s behalf.
Pace the scene slowly and deliberately — one moment per reply, never juggling multiple threads, topics, or questions. Detail should add depth to that single beat, not breadth.
Show, don't tell: convey {{char}}'s state through expression, gesture, posture, tone, and action, grounded in concrete sensory detail (light, sound, smell, texture, movement). Lead with physical action, direct dialogue, and the environment from {{char}}'s own perspective; reserve introspection or deep realizations for moments of real emotional weight.
Vary your structure — don't close every reply with a quiet observation or philosophical note. End on a natural pause that invites {{user}} to act; never summarize, wrap up, or pad a turn to fill space. Ask a question only when {{char}} genuinely would in the moment — one at most, never a checklist — and meet {{user}}'s own questions with thoughtful, in-character replies.

threads.title: Bad Habits And Formatting Issues Lets Talk So Others Can Learn Get Feedback

messages.author: Tobi Tobi
messages.content:
Yo! Noticing a lot of trends of late I think are tied to newer users and users not adjusting their private bots when posting publicly. Figured we could chat about these and similar issues so people who are curious about how to improve their bots can have a cheat sheet so to speak, especially given all the new feature updates of late.

If i write a text fomat code, remove dots for the spicy chat text boxes to use them. 
Big ones I see a lot in public bots:

- bot was clearly private previously and instead of swapping in the user-auto-populate cue {.{user.}}  they leave something like… Victoria or Alex or Kyle, clearly either the bkt author’s name or the name of the oc they were using. This actually negatively effects the bot’s functionality by confusing it, even with edits. This has a high chance of the bot spazzing out and thinking the user is schrodinger’s character and creating a ghost character or just flat out trying to default to the original character the author was writing with in mind.

- information in the bot greeting like the bot author is talking to the user. Things like “first bot”, “stole from CharAI”, “follow me for more”, etc etc. it can and often does lead to at some point the bot breaking character to do OOC stuff like it is still the author talking to the user.

- people clearly not using the bot definition section, the scenario section, ANYTHING other than the greeting to define the bot. It seriously negatively impacts the bot and can lead to more issues further on.

- extremely overly specific physical descriptions of the user in the greeting or definition or something else the author has written. This confuses the bot, which will be trying to pull from the persona but then have encoded information that contradicts it. I’ve had incidents where this flat out creates “ghost” characters where the user persona and the persona the bot was written to interact with become 2 characters with the same name.

messages.author: TorinthiaKyna
messages.content:
The LLM's latch onto negatives like that of candy. Thus telling them, 'Don't use', is effectively that of the same as speaking, "DO IT".

The better, and far more effective method, is to word such in this manner:

{{char}} avoids using — and will use either ; or ...

This can be either an command, or pinned in the memory, which aids in stopping such behavior.
In turn, check to ensure that the greeting does not have such AI generated aspects, edit and correct before making the first post.
Most LLM's will stop if these are removed or corrected after three posts.
If the LLM starts again, simply edit and most LLM's will remember and not enact again for a time.
The most effective is a combination of the above.
